acceptance_criteria.criterion: '{for: $RECORD in: $SOURCE}' translates to '{% for record in source %}'
'{for: $RECORD in: $SOURCE break_at: 5}' translates to '{% for record in source[:5] %}'
'{for: $RECORD in: $SOURCE break_at: $LIMIT}' translates to '{% for record in source[:limit] %}'
All variable names in output are consistently lowercase

summary: Rewrote ForTranslation.translate() to produce {% for loopVar in sourceVar %} using formatVariableName() for lowercase output.
break_at: N handled via [:N] Jinja2 loop slicing; variable break_at formatted through formatVariableName() as well.
Tests in ForTests.php cover simple loop, numeric break_at, variable break_at, and lowercase assertion.
All acceptance criteria met; full test suite and PHPStan level 9 pass.

comments.note: ForTranslation was a complete stub. The replace was clean — code follows the same patterns as other HubL translation classes. The Velocity ForTranslation's break-at mechanism (count-based break in the loop body) differs fundamentally from HubL's slice approach [:N]; a comment in the source distinguishes the two strategies for future maintainers.

summary: All 4 acceptance criteria verified via ForTests. Simple loop, numeric break_at, variable break_at, and lowercase enforcement all pass.
Full regression suite (309 tests, 1352 assertions) passes with no failures.
PHPStan level 9: no new violations in the modified files.

comments.note: All 4 AC confirmed via ForTests. Simple loop, numeric break_at ([:N]), variable break_at ([:var]), and lowercase-only output all verified. ForTranslation.php is clean; break_at type dispatch correctly handles both Variable and int cases.

summary: All four acceptance criteria are met.
Implementation is clean, correctly typed, and PHPStan-level-9 compliant.
One non-blocking finding: two unused imports should be removed. No blocking issues.

comments.note: sprintf '{%% for %s in %s %%}' pattern correctly double-escapes the percent signs to produce literal {% %} delimiters. Clean and idiomatic.

Two unused imports remain in ForTranslation.php: Mailcode_Parser_Statement_Tokenizer_Token_Number and Mailcode_Parser_Statement_Tokenizer_Token_Variable. These appear to be leftovers from a draft that used token introspection before switching to the higher-level getBreakAt() API. Should be removed in a cleanup pass. Non-blocking.

Type dispatch (instanceof Variable / is_int) cleanly handles both break_at variants. Silent no-op if neither branch matches is safe: the upstream command validates break_at before translation. PHPStan level 9 confirms no untyped paths.
Test covers simple loop, numeric break_at ([:13]), variable break_at with dot-notation ([:foo.bar]), and explicit case-normalization. All runCommands pattern is used correctly.

summary: Updated docs/user-guide/translate-hubl.md: moved {for} from 'Not supported' to 'Fully supported', added notes block documenting simple loop syntax, numeric break_at (Jinja2 slice [:N]), variable break_at ([:var]), lowercase variable enforcement, and a callout that {break} inside {for} remains unsupported.
Updated docs/agents/project-manifest/constraints.md: added 'for' to the HubL partial coverage list.
